key_insight: A4-MR is a 3D MRI foundation model that aligns images and text at the anatomical level and learns separate representations for healthy and abnormal anatomy, improving localization, segmentation, and abnormality detection.
clinical_relevance: This could help build a single MRI model that supports anatomy localization and downstream tasks more robustly across real-world clinical cases, including pathology-aware applications.
method: Pretrained on ~50,000 MRI studies and 491,000 series, with about half paired to radiology reports.
Uses large-scale noisy labels to learn anatomy localization and anatomical image-text alignment.
Learns distinct healthy vs abnormal anatomy representations for pathology-aware modeling.
evidence_signal: In abstract-level evaluation, A4-MR outperformed prior foundation models, including +1.7 AUROC for abnormality detection, +1.4 Dice over MedNeXt for knee segmentation, and near-best performance on abdominal organ segmentation.
watch_item: Results are promising, but performance may depend on the quality and diversity of the pretraining data, and clinical deployment would still need external validation across sites, scanners, and MRI protocols.
paper_title: A4-MR: Abnormality-aware Anatomical Alignment for MR
